description: Images, liṅgas and shrines that break, move, sweat, weep, fall or speak without cause portend the destruction of the king and the land.

Portents are heavenly (anomalies of planets and asterisms), atmospheric (meteors, thunderclaps, winds, halos, phantom cities, rainbows) and earthly (from moving and fixed things); they are 'a change of nature' announcing calamity from men's misdeeds.
The teachers of 'divine sight' (divya-dṛś) declared the true cause of eclipses; no one who is not a seer can cross, even in mind, the ocean of Kālapuruṣa.

Varāhamihira received the grace of a boon from the Sun at Kāpitthaka and composed his horā with a mind made clear by bowing at the feet of the Sun, the seers and his teacher (the tradition's account of his realization).
Comets (ketu) of many kinds — heavenly, atmospheric and earthly — whose appearance, colour, tail and direction foretell famine, war, the death of kings or prosperity (BS 11).
Earthquakes are classed by the asterism in which they occur and by their presiding powers (wind, fire, Indra, Varuṇa), each foretelling specific results (BS 32).
The tradition's claim: the consultant's own leaf, written by a seer, is found through the thumb-impression and questions and read aloud with his name and those of his family.
